text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finland is drafting legislation that will require real estate businesses and betting shops to reported suspected money laundering.

- The Paper Workers Union supports the government's economic policy, but the problems of the paper sector must be resolved, says union chief Jarmo Lahteenmaki, calling for sector-level wage talks as opposed to a comprehensive deal. @
- Members of the Finnish Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK) consider tax relief more important than wage increases, a STTK survey shows.
- Finns' opposition to nuclear power has softened during the 1990s -- now 50 percent oppose building more nuclear capacity, while 47 percent are in favour, a poll shows.
- Helsinki area inhabitants are more highly educated than people in other parts of Finland, and residents of Kauniainen are among the best-educated Europeans, statistics show.
- Finnish chicken eggs are believed to have less salmonella than European eggs, and exports to Denmark have began. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- There are no real inflation pressures on the horizon, and Finland is now recovering from a period of deflation, says Merita Bank chief economist Juha Ahtola.

- The strong dollar has drawn Finnish companies to overseas markets, giving them a competitive edge which helps cover the costs of etatablishing operations, says Lauri Virkkunen, commercial counsellor in New York.
- The hotel and catering sector is seen headed for tough pay negotiations; one of the stickiest problems is the widespread use of temporary staff, sector representatives say. @
- The Finnish construction industry was prepared for growing demand during the summer holiday season, and has faced no equipment bottlenecks as in previous summers.
AAMULEHTI
- It is too early for the Green party to choose a presidential candidate for the elections in 2000, says the party's European Parliament representative Heidi Hautala.
- Large numbers of Finns are travelling abroad again, with an increase of 14 percent on last year, statistics show. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Former U.S president Jimmy Carter is on an unofficial visit to Finland, fishing at Konnevesi; his wife Rosalynn is taking part in an international symposium on mental health.
DEMARI
- All powers of the president should be limited, and the presidency should function as an institution, says Social Democrat parliamentary group leader Erkki Tuomioja.
- A poll shows 43 percent of the STTK union members are opposed to Finland joining European monetary and economic union, EMU, while 34 percent are in favour. @
--Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
